item.title: Physics-guided explainable machine learning and uncertainty quantification for predicting unconfined compressive strength of nano shale–quicklime stabilized kaolin clay
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Arash Aminaee, Abolfazl Soltani, Abolfazl Baghbani, Parisa Salehan, Hossam Abuel-Naga, Pijush Samui
Data-driven prediction of stabilized-soil strength is often constrained by small experimental datasets, leakage between related specimens, and limited physical interpretability. This study develops an explainable, uncertainty-aware framework to predict the unconfined compressive strength (UCS) of nano shale–quicklime stabilized kaolin. A specimen-level database of 180 measurements from 36 mixture–curing conditions was analyzed using multiple linear regression (MLR), support vector regression (SVR), random forest (RF), XGBoost, CatBoost, and backpropagation artificial neural network (BP-ANN), with nonlinear models optimized by particle swarm optimization and evaluated through nested GroupKFold cross-validation. item.title: MindTopo: Can Foundation Models Reason in Topological Space?
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Yunfei Ge, Anbang Liu, Qineng Wang, Johnalbert Garnica, Jianwen Lyu, Zihan Wang, Reuben Tan, Jianfeng Gao, Ruohan Zhang, Yining Hong, Jiajun Wu, Manling Li
arXiv:2609.11900v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spatial reasoning depends not only on metric properties such as distance, angle, and shape, but also on topological relations that remain invariant under continuous deformation. Cognitive science identifies these relations as foundational to spatial understanding, yet foundation-model evaluations largely focus on metric or viewpoint-dependent relations. We introduce MindTopo, a benchmark of topological intuition across five properties grounded in cognitive science and formal topology: continuity, separation, order, enclosure, and knots. MindTopo evaluates each property at two cognitive levels. Reasoning asks a model to identify topological relations or infer how they change. item.title: Quantum Federated Digital Twin Framework with Explainable Multi-Agent Intelligence for Autonomous Engineering Management
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Nilesh Vasant Ingale, Mahesh Dhande, Pankaj Deshmukh
Autonomous engineering management increasingly depends on distributed digital twins that must learn, coordinate, and justify decisions across geographically separated industrial sites without exposing proprietary operating data. Existing solutions address these needs only in isolation: federated learning preserves data locality but offers no formal guarantee against gradient-based information leakage; multi-agent reinforcement learning coordinates distributed controllers but rarely explains its own decisions; and digital twins provide high-fidelity virtual representations but are seldom coupled to a decision layer that can act autonomously while remaining auditable by human engineers. item.title: Halide Perovskite Trilayer Metasurfaces for Ultrabright and Wide-Gamut Structural Color
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Rukon Uddin
We present an all-perovskite, gradient-index trilayer metasurface for reflective structural color based on a truncated-cone meta-atom comprising a black-phase α-CsPbI₃ core between two MAPbCl₃ cladding layers. The design translates the multilayer gradient-index concept previously demonstrated with GaP/TiO₂ into a chemically related halide-perovskite platform. Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations show that, with the three-layer heights fixed at 90/100/80 nm, the palette can be generated primarily by scaling the lateral radii and lattice period. Seven representative colors are obtained with peak reflectance near unity in the reported simulations and resonance peaks spanning 470–630 nm. item.title: Competitive Displacement Fluorescence Biosensor Based on Aptamer-Peptide Conjugates for Simultaneous Detection of Pb 2+ and Cd 2+ in Rice
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Liling Hao, Jiaqi Han, Jiahao Sha, Xu Jin, Kaimin Peng, Fei Xu
Lead (Pb2+) and cadmium (Cd2+) frequently co-occur in agricultural products, making rapid methods for their sensitive and simultaneous detection highly necessary. Current fluorescence methods often rely on signal amplification, which increases assay time and complexity. To achieve rapid and amplification-free detection, we developed a fast and sensitive fluorescence biosensor by anchoring high affinity aptamer-peptide conjugates (APCs) onto tetrahedral DNA nanostructures (TDNs) functionalized Fe3O4/Au magnetic nanoparticles. In the presence of targets, Pb2+ and Cd2+ competitively displace the corresponding fluorescently labeled APCs from the magnetic nanoparticles into the supernatant. item.title: Adsorption and photo-Fenton catalytic degradation of Orange II dye over cobalt ferrite nanoparticles and almond shell biochar
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Martina Lorente, Inés Salvador, Ana Beatriz Fossati, Analía Verónica Russo
The purpose of this work is to synthesize and characterize new materials based on magnetic nanoparticles and almond shell biochar, and to evaluate their ability to remove Orange II dye from water sources. For this purpose, different systems were prepared: magnetic cobalt ferrite nanoparticles (MNP), MNP synthesized on almond shell biochar (BMNP) and a mechanical mixture of MNP and biochar (MM). These systems were characterized by X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, magnetic measurements and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, revealing different structural properties for the three samples. item.title: Language-Augmented Semantic Priors for B-Spline Surface Fitting
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Yunzhong Lou, Yusheng Luo, Jiahao Li, Yu Song, Xiangdong Zhou
arXiv:2609.11708v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The use of B-splines and Non-Uniform Rational B-Splines surfaces constitutes the mathematical foundation of contemporary computer-aided design (CAD) systems. Despite long-term progress, geometric kernels in traditional CAD still rely heavily on predetermined heuristic initialization for surface fitting and parameterization. Meanwhile, the procedural semantics and design intent encoded in modeling histories are largely ignored during geometry generation. This disconnect creates a gap between high-level design intent and solver-executable geometric configuration, often leading to suboptimal and semantically inconsistent fitting results. item.title: LAMP: LLM-Augmented Multi-Task Spectral Prediction for Au-GaN Metasurfaces
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Xumin Gao, Hangqi Ge, Ting Wan, Yu Wang, Zheng Shi
Accurate multi-response spectral prediction is essential for metasurface performance evaluation, design-space exploration, and structural optimization. However, the underlying structure-to-spectrum mapping is highly nonlinear and requires the joint modeling of multiple optical responses over a broad wavelength range. Conventional neural predictors are effective at learning quantitative structure-to-spectrum relationships, whereas large language models (LLMs) can provide contextual representations of structural configurations. These two modeling paradigms, however, have largely been investigated independently. To bridge this gap, we propose LLM-augmented multi-task spectral prediction (LAMP), a dual-branch framework that integrates a spectral sequence encoder with a frozen LLM-based prompt…

item.title: RL-Assisted A-Teams for Adaptive Algorithm Selection in UGV-UAV Route Optimization
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Subramanian Ramasamy, Md Safwan Mondal, James D. Humann, James M. Dotterweich, Pranav Bhounsule
Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are capable of monitoring large areas but are constrained by limited battery life. Collaborating with Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs) can greatly extend the endurance of UAVs by utilizing UGVs as mobile charging platforms. Integrating Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs) enables effective long-duration surveillance over large areas, especially where real-time adaptability is essential. However, this also increases the complexity of routing these heterogeneous vehicles. Therefore, developing an efficient UGV-UAV routing framework is essential to ensure real-time adaptability, enabling them to respond effectively to dynamic changes. item.title: Automating Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) Formulation Generation from Natural Language
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Niloy Kumar Mondal, Md Rizwan Parvez
arXiv:2609.10629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) is a central formulation for combinatorial optimization and has gained increasing attention due to its compatibility with quantum, hybrid quantum-classical, and quantum-inspired solvers. However, translating natural-language problem descriptions into correct QUBO formulations remains difficult, requiring the identification of binary variables, constraints, objective functions, penalty terms, and suitable penalty weights. This process is time-consuming and often demands substantial domain expertise. item.title: Physicists turn classical light into a quantum machine for information processing
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Quantum computers promise to tackle problems that are extraordinarily difficult for today's computers. But there is a major obstacle: quantum systems are notoriously fragile. Noise, loss and even tiny disturbances can destroy the delicate behavior that gives them their power. Building systems with many quantum particles is also extremely challenging.
